Output of `forgecycle help task <command>` for ForgeCycle 0.6.0.

## forgecycle task run

Start a Planner–Builder–Reviewer task run for one task.

```text
Usage: forgecycle task run [options] <task.md>

Start a Planner–Builder–Reviewer task run for one task.

Arguments:
  <task.md>          The task file; YAML front matter under forgecycle may set
                     approval, base, and checkpoints

Options:
  --policy NAME      Use routing policy NAME (default: the configured
                     default_policy)
  --base REF         Start from Git revision REF (default: HEAD)
  --approval POLICY  autonomous, plan-and-final, every-turn, or custom
  --planner ID       Use candidate ID as Planner for this invocation only
  --builder ID       Use candidate ID as Builder for this invocation only; not
                     a read-only candidate
  --reviewer ID      Use candidate ID as Reviewer for this invocation only
  --auto-resume      Resume once in this process after a stop that a plain task
                     resume fixes (see below)
  -h, --help         Show this help

task run creates the branch forgecycle/task/<task-run-id> and a worktree under
.forgecycle/worktrees/<task-run-id>, and stores the task run under
.forgecycle/task-runs/<task-run-id>/. Files listed in worktree.copy_ignored are
copied into the worktree with mode 0600.

--planner, --builder, and --reviewer each replace that role's candidate list
with one candidate listed for that role in the active policy, to switch agents
(for example, one that ran out of tokens) without editing the configuration.

When the task run stops (exit 20, 21, or 22), it prints a stop block:
'forgecycle: stop:' lines with the status, stop kind, reason, resume target,
and files to inspect, then 'forgecycle: next:' lines with the suggested
commands. task resume, task approve, and task reject print the same block when
the task run stops again.

A stopped or interrupted task run keeps the repository reservation, so another
task run is refused with exit 21: 'Repository is reserved by run
<task-run-id>'. The lines after the error say how to free it: 'forgecycle:
stop: reserved_by=<task-run-id> status=…' and 'forgecycle: next:' lines with
that task run's next commands, then task abandon to discard it. task resume,
task approve, task reject, and task abandon print the same lines when another
task run holds the reservation.

Ctrl-C or SIGTERM stops the running agent CLI (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 10
seconds) and leaves the task run interrupted, or stops a running gate's process
group, runs its cleanup, and records gate_failure (interrupted). The stop block
follows, --auto-resume does not act on it, and the command ends by the signal
(exit status 130 or 143). A second Ctrl-C exits at once.

A turn ends with the agent's final message. On Linux and macOS, processes a
turn started in the worktree or in the task-run directory (which holds its
EVIDENCE_DIR) and left running are stopped when it ends (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL
after 10 seconds), with a 'forgecycle: warning: stopped N process(es)' line
naming each one and its directory.

forgecycle pause, from another terminal, stops the task run once its current
turn ends instead: it records the stop kind pause_requested, resumes into the
turn it was about to start, and exits 21. forgecycle unpause continues it.

A command refused because another process advances the same task run ('Run is
already being advanced by process <pid>', exit 21) prints 'forgecycle: stop:
task_run=<task-run-id> process=<pid>' and 'forgecycle: next: forgecycle task
status <task-run-id>': wait until that process stops. Roadmap commands do the
same with roadmap_run= and roadmap status.

--auto-resume acts on a stop whose recovery is a plain task resume with no
input: unaccepted_head, review_invariant, gate_failure (interrupted), and
agent_failure except quota_exhausted, rate_limited, authentication_error,
config_error, and worktree_mutated. It resumes at most once between two
accepted handoffs, and each automatic resume is a billed model call. The stop
block prints first, then 'forgecycle: info: auto-resume: <stop-kind>
(<detail>); resuming into <phase> (turn N)'. A stop that remains after an
automatic resume, with no accepted handoff since, adds 'forgecycle: stop:
auto_resume=used turn=<n>'.

See also: forgecycle help task status, forgecycle help task resume
```

## forgecycle task status

Show a task run's state, its stop, and what to do next.

```text
Usage: forgecycle task status [--json] <task-run-id>

Show a task run's state, its stop, and what to do next.

Arguments:
  <task-run-id>  A task run ID, as task run prints it and status lists it

Options:
  --json         Print the stored state document for scripts; stop_kind and
                 stop_detail classify a stop
  -h, --help     Show this help

task status prints the state, phase, branch, and worktree. A stopped task run
also shows:
  - its reason and stop kind, for example agent_failure (quota_exhausted) or
    needs_human
  - the phase it resumes into and the role that reads feedback
  - an Auto-resume line when an automatic resume already ran with no accepted
    handoff since
  - the latest handoff, events.log, and the latest evidence directory
  - Next lines with the suggested commands; steps marked (human decision) need
    a human

A task run left in an active state by a killed process, or by Ctrl-C or SIGTERM
during an agent turn, is reported as interrupted. A task run started by a
roadmap run shows a Roadmap run line with the roadmap task ID. A done task run
shows its result.md.

See also: forgecycle help status
```

## forgecycle task resume

Continue a paused, blocked, failed, or interrupted task run.

```text
Usage: forgecycle task resume [options] <task-run-id>

Continue a paused, blocked, failed, or interrupted task run.

Arguments:
  <task-run-id>    A task run ID, as task run prints it and status lists it

Options:
  --feedback FILE  Add the written human direction in FILE
  --planner ID     Use candidate ID as Planner for this invocation only
  --builder ID     Use candidate ID as Builder for this invocation only; not a
                   read-only candidate
  --reviewer ID    Use candidate ID as Reviewer for this invocation only
  --auto-resume    As for task run: resume once more after a stop that a plain
                   task resume fixes
  -h, --help       Show this help

task resume re-enters the phase recorded as resume_state and prints it with the
role that reads the feedback, for example 'resuming into building (turn 4);
feedback 003-human-feedback.md will be read by Builder'. An interrupted task
run (its process was killed, or Ctrl-C stopped an agent turn, so no stop was
recorded) re-enters planning if it was planning, and reviewing otherwise, so
Reviewer reconciles an interrupted Builder turn. Missing worktree.copy_ignored
files are restored before the next turn.

Approval gates take task approve or task reject instead of --feedback. Feedback
that answers a needs_human stop of a roadmap run's task run is also appended to
the roadmap run's decisions as an H decision, quoting the Planner's or
Reviewer's question, so the task runs it starts later receive it.

With --planner, --builder, or --reviewer, name the role that acts next. The
stop block's 'forgecycle: next:' lines print the matching command, for example:
  forgecycle task resume <task-run-id> --builder <candidate-id>

--auto-resume acts on the same stops as for task run: unaccepted_head,
review_invariant, gate_failure (interrupted), and agent_failure except
quota_exhausted, rate_limited, authentication_error, config_error, and
worktree_mutated. Each automatic resume is a billed model call.

See also: forgecycle help task run, forgecycle help task approve
```

## forgecycle task approve

Approve a task run waiting at an approval gate.

```text
Usage: forgecycle task approve <task-run-id>

Approve a task run waiting at an approval gate.

Arguments:
  <task-run-id>  A task run ID, as task run prints it and status lists it

Options:
  -h, --help     Show this help

Use it for a task run paused after its plan or before its final result.

See also: forgecycle help task reject
```

## forgecycle task reject

Reject an approval gate with written feedback.

```text
Usage: forgecycle task reject <task-run-id> <feedback.md>

Reject an approval gate with written feedback.

Arguments:
  <task-run-id>  A task run ID, as task run prints it and status lists it
  <feedback.md>  The written feedback, stored as an immutable handoff

Options:
  -h, --help     Show this help

The feedback returns direction to Planner at the plan gate, or to Reviewer at
the final gate.

See also: forgecycle help task approve
```

## forgecycle task abandon

Stop a task run and release its repository reservation.

```text
Usage: forgecycle task abandon <task-run-id>

Stop a task run and release its repository reservation.

Arguments:
  <task-run-id>  A task run ID, as task run prints it and status lists it

Options:
  -h, --help     Show this help

Its branch, worktree, and stored artifacts remain for inspection; task clean
removes the worktree.
```

## forgecycle task clean

Remove a finished task run's worktree.

```text
Usage: forgecycle task clean <task-run-id>

Remove a finished task run's worktree.

Arguments:
  <task-run-id>  A task run ID, as task run prints it and status lists it

Options:
  -h, --help     Show this help

The task run must be done, failed, or abandoned. Its branch and stored
artifacts remain.
```
